title: ACA s. 9 — Interim measures by Court (ACA s. 9)

content.overview: Section 9 empowers a party to apply to the Court for interim measures before or during arbitral proceedings or at any time after the making of the arbitral award but before it is enforced. The Court may grant measures for preservation, interim custody, securing the amount in dispute, detention or inspection of property, interim injunction, appointment of a receiver, and other just and convenient reliefs. After the tribunal is constituted, the Court should ordinarily not entertain a section 9 application if the tribunal can grant efficacious relief under section 17.
content.glance: Court interim measures before, during, or after arbitration until enforcement; residual after tribunal constitution if s. 17 is efficacious.
content.study: Section 9 is an express Part I gateway for court interim relief. It is available even before commencement of arbitral proceedings. Once the tribunal is constituted, section 17 is preferred where it can grant efficacious relief.

sections.heading: When available
sections.body: Before or during arbitral proceedings, or after the award but before enforcement.

sections.heading: Types of measures
sections.body: Preservation, custody, security, inspection, injunction, receiver, and other just and convenient reliefs as provided.

sections.heading: Relationship with section 17
sections.body: After tribunal constitution, Court should ordinarily not act under s. 9 if the tribunal can grant efficacious relief under s. 17.

cases.name: Sundaram Finance Ltd. v. NEPC India Ltd.
cases.facts: Application for interim measures under section 9 before the arbitral tribunal was constituted.
cases.issue: Can the Court grant interim measures under section 9 before the commencement of arbitral proceedings?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 9 can be invoked before arbitral proceedings have commenced; the Court has power to grant interim measures to preserve the subject-matter.
cases.holding: Interim relief under section 9 is available even before the tribunal is in place, subject to the statutory framework.
cases.relevance: Foundational authority on pre-commencement section 9 relief.

cases.name: ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India Ltd. v. Essar Bulk Terminal Ltd.
cases.facts: Parallel section 9 applications and interaction with the tribunal's powers under section 17 after the 2015 amendments.
cases.issue: How do Court-ordered interim measures under section 9 interact with the tribunal's section 17 powers once the tribunal is constituted?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Once the arbitral tribunal is constituted, the Court should ordinarily not entertain a section 9 application if the tribunal can grant efficacious relief under section 17.
cases.holding: Clarified the residual role of the Court under section 9 after tribunal constitution.
cases.relevance: Key post-2015 authority on the balance between sections 9 and 17.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can section 9 be invoked before arbitral proceedings commence?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Yes. Sundaram Finance holds that section 9 is available before the commencement of arbitral proceedings.

examTips: Pre-commencement relief available; after tribunal constitution prefer s. 17 if efficacious.

enhancement.definition: Section 9 empowers the Court to grant interim measures in aid of arbitration.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Court interim measures before, during, or after arbitration until enforcement; residual after tribunal constitution if s. 17 is efficacious.
